Abstract.AbstractText: The interfacial electronic structure of Fe3O4/BaTiO3 heterostructures was investigated using first-principles calculations. Owing to the two TiO-polarization directions, FeBO-terminated models show different interfacial binding strengths. Compared with the OTi-FeBO model, the TiO-FeBO model shows a spin polarization of 100% due to the hybridization effect of Ti 3d and FeB 3d at the Fermi level, which can be modulated by the electric field and TiO polarization directions. Negative electric field can control the strength of the hybridization of the interfacial Ti and O with FeB, but the positive electric field has no significant effect on it. The tunable high spin polarization at Fe3O4/BaTiO3 interfaces has potential applications in spintronic devices.
